text: The exhibition "For the Freedom of a People," dedicated to the 150th anniversary of the April Uprising, was opened at the Bulgarian Cultural and Information Center in Skopje (28.04.2026 20:35)

The exhibition "For the Freedom of a People," prepared by the St. St. Cyril and Methodius National Library and the Archives State Agency on the occasion of the 150th anniversary of the outbreak of the April Uprising, was opened at the Bulgarian Cultural and Information Center in Skopje.

„Today, we are not just opening an exhibition. Today, we are opening a door to memory, to that fateful April of 1876, when the Bulgarian people took their destiny into their own hands, driven by an irresistible yearning for freedom, dignity, and national self-determination.... The April Uprising is not merely a historical fact. It is a moral pinnacle. It is a symbol of self-sacrifice, of unity, and of the unyielding spirit of a people who chose freedom over fear. The exhibition we are opening today is a bridge of sorts between the past, the present, and the future. Through documents and narratives, it reminds us not only of the events but also of the human destinies behind them – the destinies of ordinary people who became heroes, to whom we owe our Freedom,“ stated Antonia Veleva, Director of the Bulgarian Cultural and Information Center.

In video addresses, those present in the indoor gallery of the Bulgarian Cultural and Information Center were addressed by the Director of the National Library, Kalina Ivanova, and the Director of the State Archives Agency, Mikhail Gruev, as well as Milen Mihov, curator and one of the compilers of the documentary exhibition.

The exhibition includes over 130 documents – minutes, letters, telegrams, proclamations, certificates, and others – which illustrate the preparation, course, suppression, and consequences of the April Uprising. They also reveal the international response to the uprising, with Ottoman Turkish documents being particularly important as they show the perspective of the local and central Ottoman authorities. The exhibition presents both well-known and little-known documents, some of which are being displayed for the first time. It traces the events in all revolutionary districts, the role of the Bulgarian emigration, and the international response to the uprising, and Skopje is the first place outside of Bulgaria where it is being presented.

Before the opening of the exhibition "For the Freedom of a People", which will be displayed at the Bulgarian Cultural and Information Center in Skopje, children from the preschool group of the "Zdravei" Sunday school participated in an open lesson related to the April Uprising.
